top: rise in urea imports in Apr–Nov FY25–26, while domestic urea output fell 3.7% even as record foodgrain production kept demand high.
was the April 2026 urea tender price, against $419/t in Nov 2025 and $447/t in Jun 2026, so import costs swung by more than the subsidy planning could absorb.

sections.h2: Urea sales rose 2.3% while domestic urea output fell 3.7%

chart.title: Domestic output fell in urea and DAP while sales held
chart.sub: Change in Apr–Nov FY 2025–26 versus the prior year, %.
chart.source: Department of Fertilizers; Fertiliser Association of India.

sections.means: Imports, not new domestic capacity, filled the extra demand from record cropping, with urea imports up 120% to 7.17 MT and DAP import dependence rising from 56% to 67%.
sections.todo: Lock in firm LNG on long-term fixed-price contracts ring-fenced for fertiliser feedstock, so plant-level gas allocation is insulated from spot-market and Hormuz-transit shocks.

sections.h2: Urea tender prices went from $419/t to $959/t and back to $447/t in seven months

chart.title: India paid more than double the pre-crisis price at the April peak
chart.sub: India's urea tender prices, USD per tonne cfr.
chart.source: Argus Media; Profercy; StoneX; Business Standard.

sections.means: The swing came from China's export policy and a Hormuz closure thousands of kilometres away, not from India's own demand, and it reversed in the same tender mechanism within seven weeks.
sections.todo: Weigh domestic production against imports using the full range of tender prices, not a single snapshot, because the volatility is the real story.

sections.h2: Domestic urea beats every import tender only below about $10.3/MMBtu gas

chart.title: Modelled domestic cost passes the $419/t cheapest tender between $9 and $14 gas
chart.sub: Modelled domestic urea cost by feedstock gas price scenario, USD per tonne.
chart.source: Author's calculation in the original: (gas price x 30 MMBtu/tonne) + $110/tonne.

sections.means: At APM gas of $7/MMBtu modelled domestic urea at about $320/t undercuts every tender this cycle, but at crisis spot LNG of about $20/MMBtu it costs about $710/t and only beats the April peak.
sections.todo: Accelerate the coal-route urea model, starting with Talcher by June 2027, to sidestep the $10.3/MMBtu crossover risk for that capacity.

sections.h2: Central substitution needs 24.9 mmscmd, above 19.2 mmscmd of well-connected spare

chart.title: Central and high substitution exceed spare capacity at Dahej and Hazira
chart.sub: Incremental gas demand by scenario against spare regasification capacity at Dahej and Hazira, mmscmd.
chart.source: Author's calculation; PNGRB, Optimising LNG Supplies from Terminals in India, December 2024.

sections.means: National spare capacity of 105.5 mmscmd looks ample, but most of it sits at terminals poorly connected to the fertiliser plant clusters, and Dahej is already at 89.9% utilisation.
sections.todo: Complete pipeline connectivity from the east-coast terminals, especially Dhamra, and resolve third-party access at Mundra before relying on LNG-fed substitution.
